notes: Austrian wines are mostly dry whites, often from Grüner Veltliner, with sweet wines around the Neusiedlersee.
Blaufränkisch gives deeply colored reds with dark fruit, peppery spice and moderate to high acidity, and Zweigelt fresh, fruity reds.
In Mittelburgenland DAC, basic Blaufränkisch shows little or no oak, while Reserve wines show noticeable oak and at least 13% alcohol.
Eisenberg's iron-rich red soils give Blaufränkisch a distinct spiciness.
Wines are rarely given new oak or malolactic, and are fuller bodied, closer to Alsace than to Germany.
The best Smaragd wines can age more than 20 years.
Weinviertel DAC is aromatic and spicy, with pepper notes and no botrytis or oak.
Weinviertel DAC Reserve is dry, full bodied and spicy, and may show subtle botrytis and oak.
On the Wagram, Grüner Veltliner is a little fuller and more aromatic.
